content:
<other>: The Subcommittee on Research and Technology will come to order. Today's hearing examines H.R. 6110, the AI Infrastructure Act, and the federal permitting process for large-scale data centers. The chair recognizes the gentlewoman from California.
<Rep. Priya Raman>: Thank you, Mr. Chairman. I support this bill, and I want to be clear about why. We are going to build this capacity somewhere, and I would rather it be built here under our labor and environmental standards than overseas. But support is not a blank check. Section 4 still has no binding water-use disclosure, and I will offer an amendment to add one before I vote for final passage.
<Rep. Thomas Beaumont>: I thank the gentlewoman. I will be brief. Federal permitting reform is overdue and this bill does it; I support it without reservation. What I do not support is the amendment she describes. Every disclosure mandate becomes a lawsuit, and every lawsuit becomes a five-year delay. We should pass the bill clean.
<Rep. Harold Finch>: My district has two of these campuses under construction right now. They are the largest private investment the north state has seen in a generation. So yes, I support the permitting title. I also want the record to show I am not persuaded that we need a federal AI licensing regime on top of it; that is a separate bill and I remain opposed to it.
<Rep. Mei-Ling Tsao>: I respect my colleagues, but I cannot support H.R. 6110 as written. Our groundwater basin is already in overdraft. Until this bill contains an enforceable water cap, not a disclosure, a cap, I am a no.
<Rep. Alicia Marquez>: I want to move to a different subject for a moment, because the chairman has allowed it. On the background-check bill, H.R. 4410, I will say again what I said in March: we cannot keep burying children while weapons of war are sold without so much as a background check. I will vote yes when it reaches the floor.
<other>: The gentlewoman's time has expired. The subcommittee stands in recess.
